sources.title: Hideo Kojima (Q315577) -- verified live via the Wikidata API (2026-10-24): English label 'Hideo Kojima', description 'Japanese video game designer (born 1963)', born 24 August 1963, no date of death, Korean label present, P18 images include 'Hideo Kojima 20100702 Japan Expo 1 (cropped).jpg'. Orientation only; not used as support for any row.

Game Developers Conference, '2009 Game Developers Choice Awards Honor Kojima For Lifetime Achievement' (announcement by GDC and Gamasutra), read in full. CANONICAL SIGNIFICANCE SOURCE: says the Lifetime Achievement Award recognises developers with an 'indelible impact on the craft'; credits Kojima with the stealth genre via 1987's Metal Gear (born of MSX hardware limits), the 1998 breakthrough of Metal Gear Solid on PlayStation, the Snatcher, Policenauts and Zone of the Enders work, Boktai's sunlight sensor cartridge as 'disruption of traditional gaming mechanics', and breaking the fourth wall with players; names earlier recipients including Miyamoto and Sid Meier. An award-body announcement: admiring and promotional in tone.

British Film Institute, 'Metal Gear Solid 3: Snake Eater 20th anniversary: Kojima's masterful tribute to spy cinema' (BFI feature), read in full: places Kojima's 1987 Metal Gear as a war game that avoids combat, quoting his 2020 BAFTA interview after receiving the BAFTA Fellowship about being against his company's instruction to make an arcade war game; describes the cinematic cutscenes, film references, the survival and camouflage mechanics of Snake Eater and the series' notorious cutscene length; notes a Konami remake in development without Kojima. A film-institute critical appreciation; admiring, with some criticism of cutscene length.

GamesBeat, 'A Brief History of Stealth Games', read in full: traces stealth game lineage from Castle Wolfenstein (1981) to Metal Gear (1987) and Metal Gear Solid (1998), says Kojima created and designed Metal Gear, incorporated core elements of Castle Wolfenstein and added more refined presentation, that its release 'didn't send shockwaves', and that Metal Gear Solid became a seminal work whose success its antecedents did not match, while crediting Tenchu and Thief for the same-year response to stealth action. Independent genre history that qualifies 'first' claims.

Kotaku, Metal Gear Solid retrospective article, read: argues that Metal Gear Solid is one of the most fondly remembered games, helped codify stealth action, and uses its structure to undercut the player's success; credits Kojima with emulating film language, such as integrating the credits into play. Independent critical retrospective that is partly critical of the series' message.

Video Games Chronicle, 'Death Stranding review round-up: critics divided on Kojima's epic' (November 2019), read in full: scores from 6 to 10 with quotes from named outlets; one reviewer finds an 'unusual and fascinating' game clogged by its creator's self-importance, another calls it Kojima's boldest and most tedious, another describes an open-world design with asynchronous cooperative multiplayer alongside a long, confusing film, another the most unique big-budget game they have played. COUNTER-VOICE source on the independence period's first game.

Game Informer, 'An Interview With Hideo Kojima' (15 June 2016), read in full: Kojima on life as an independent developer (freedom, fewer meetings, the danger of meeting fewer people, reading and film to keep his vision wide), staffing Kojima Productions from four people in December 2015, searching for an engine and facilities with Sony, the Kobo Abe stick-and-rope idea behind Death Stranding, and reconnecting with Norman Reedus and Guillermo del Toro. An interview: self-account, admiring interviewer.

NME, 'Death Stranding developer will stay independent as long as I'm alive says Hideo Kojima' (NME news report on his Brain Structure podcast), read in full: Kojima says the studio was funded 100 per cent out of his pocket, that he receives acquisition offers some at 'ridiculously high prices' and will not accept them, and that he won't revisit earlier franchises. Entertainment-news report quoting his own statements.

SiliconANGLE, report on the Nikkei article about Konami's working conditions and the Silent Hills cancellation (3 August 2015), read in full for context only: confirms Konami cancelled the Kojima-del Toro Silent Hills project and quotes del Toro calling the cancellation 'scorched earth'; the working-condition allegations concern Konami and were not used to score Kojima. Secondhand report of a Nikkei story.

Wikimedia Commons file page 'Hideo Kojima 20100702 Japan Expo 1 (cropped).jpg' by Georges Seguin (Okki), own work, 2 July 2010, licence GFDL and Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0/2.5/2.0/1.0 (self-published multi-licence), checked for the portrait only.

creative_originality.rationale: [src_kojima_gdc, src_kojima_bfi, src_kojima_gamesbeat, src_kojima_vgc | 1987-2019 | award body + film institute + press + critics roundup] GDC credits Metal Gear with a fresh approach to action games born of hardware limits and Boktai with an unconventional sunlight-sensor mechanic; BFI describes Metal Gear Solid 3's cinematic mash-up and survival and camouflage mechanics as innovative; critics of Death Stranding call it unusual and unique even where they dislike it. Independent genre history (GamesBeat) qualifies the 'first' claims by crediting Castle Wolfenstein, Tenchu and Thief, so the originality is real but not a sole invention. SELF-CALIBRATION (agent): reviewed as top-risk row (highest score, award-body and retrospective praise); kept because critics who dislike Death Stranding still call it unusual, and genre history independently documents new mechanics.

experimentation.rationale: [src_kojima_gdc, src_kojima_bfi, src_kojima_vgc | 2003-2019 | award body + film institute + critics roundup] Boktai's sunlight-sensor cartridge and fourth-wall-breaking play (GDC), the survival and camouflage mechanics of Snake Eater (BFI), and Death Stranding's asynchronous multiplayer open-world design that critics found polarising (VGC). Experiments are documented across independent sources; mixed outcomes are shown by the review split.

aesthetic_sensitivity.rationale: [src_kojima_bfi, src_kojima_kotaku | 2004-2019 | film institute + press] BFI describes cutscenes built with 'a sharp eye for scene composition' and a skill for directing action, with deliberate James Bond title-sequence and film homages; Kotaku credits him with emulating film language, e.g. integrating credits into play. Both are retrospective critical appreciations; the claim is an inference about a design sensibility from reviewers' reading of the work, and BFI also notes the cutscenes' notorious length.

independent_thinking.rationale: [src_kojima_bfi | 1987 | film institute quoting his 2020 BAFTA interview] Kojima says his company asked for an arcade 'Rambo' war game but he was against it and conceived a war game that avoids combat, which BFI places as the origin of the stealth approach. The behaviour is documented in outline by the genre history, but the motivation comes only from his own retrospective interview. SELF-CALIBRATION (agent): reviewed as a self-only row; lowered from 66 / 0.48 to 60 / 0.44 because the one-source, self-account basis was stronger than the row claimed.

autonomy_need.rationale: [src_kojima_gameinformer, src_kojima_nme | 2015-2021 | interview + news report] After leaving Konami he re-formed Kojima Productions as an independent studio, started from four people, and says he turned down acquisition offers and funded the studio out of his own pocket so he could 'make what I want to make'. Both sources are his own statements (an interview and a podcast); the studio's existence is independently documented but the reasons are self-reported. SELF-CALIBRATION (agent): reviewed as a self-only row; lowered from 68 / 0.5 to 62 / 0.45 because all motive evidence is self-account and the Konami split is documented only as a professional episode with conflicting company and personal accounts.

proactive_agency.rationale: [src_kojima_gameinformer, src_kojima_vgc, src_kojima_siliconangle | 2015-2019 | interview + critics roundup + news report] After the Silent Hills cancellation he announced a new studio with Sony as publishing partner in December 2015, searched for an engine, facilities and staff from a team of four, and delivered Death Stranding in 2019. The sequence is documented by outcomes and by his own interview; no independent account of how the studio was started.

risk_tolerance.rationale: [src_kojima_vgc, src_kojima_gameinformer | 2015-2019 | critics roundup + interview] He launched an independent studio and a big-budget game built on an unconventional walking, delivery and asynchronous-connection design; critics split from 6 to 10, with some calling it his boldest and also his most tedious. Dual-edged because the unconventional choice produced polarised reception. Inference from the design choices and reviews; no direct account of the risk assessment.

VOCABULARY GAP (flag for lead): the repo has no labelled game designer or game developer occupation (game_developer is on the unlabelled list), so product_designer and writer are used as the closest labelled ids (he is credited as writer and director of Death Stranding by Game Informer); fields technology and design, tag innovator and independent, archetype independent_creator are labelled. ZERO POLITICS: passes. LIVING SUBJECT: only documented public professional behaviour scored; excluded: private life, health, the Konami working-condition allegations (about the employer, reported secondhand from a Nikkei story), speculation about the reasons for the 2015 departure (sources conflict; treated only as a professional episode: Silent Hills cancelled, Konami's account differs from commentators'), his podcast's non-professional content. CANONICAL SIGNIFICANCE SOURCE: Game Developers Choice Awards 2009 Lifetime Achievement announcement (https://gdconf.com/article/2009-game-developers-choice-awards-honor-kojima-for-lifetime-achievement/). READ (9 sources + portrait record): GDC, BFI, GamesBeat, Kotaku, VGC roundup, Game Informer, NME, SiliconANGLE (context only). PERSPECTIVES: award body, film institute, independent genre history, retrospective critics, Death Stranding reviewers, self-interviews. COUNTER-VOICES: GamesBeat qualifying the first-stealth claims, VGC reviewers calling the work self-important and tedious, Kotaku on the series' message. NOT opened: GameSpot (403) on the Konami split, Eurogamer/Guardian reviews, GDC 2009 talk itself (self material), Wikipedia, Nikkei original. PORTRAIT: Commons file is the photographer's own work with multiple licences (GFDL plus CC BY-SA 3.0/2.5/2.0/1.0), dated 2 July 2010 at Japan Expo, created by an identified Commons contributor; Commons carries a personality-rights notice template; no conflicting institutional notice exists. Original is 2851 x 3312; saved as the 960 px Commons thumbnail (downscale only). SELF-CALIBRATION: rows reviewed: creative_originality (76, kept: critics who dislike Death Stranding still call it unusual, and independent genre history documents the mechanics), independent_thinking (lowered 66/0.48 to 60/0.44, single self-account source), autonomy_need (lowered 68/0.5 to 62/0.45, self-statements only).
